title: Machine Learning Research Engineer
text:
Orbital Industries is building the AI Industrial: a new category of company that solves the physical world's hardest problems with frontier AI.
Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system for science and engineering. CurieOS connects three disciplines that have historically worked in silos — materials discovery, hardware product development and deployment engineering — into a single AI orchestration platform. No other company operates across this full lifecycle.
We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.
Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.
As a Machine Learning Research Engineer at Orbital, you will architect cutting-edge AI systems for the multi-scale design of physical technologies. When we say multi-scale, we mean it: we build world-class foundation models for simulating both the microscopic motion of atoms and the macroscopic flow of liquids in 1GW data centers. We then co-design across these different scales using the ingenuity of our scientists and engineers, augmented with best-in-class domain agents.
In this role you will set exceptionally high technical standards and drive projects from prototype through to production deployment. First and foremost, we want to work with someone with a love of craftsmanship, continual learning, and building systems that scale. We also value low ego, and a genuine passion for using AI to solve major global industrial technology challenges.
Key Responsibilities
Set the technical bar and ensure engineering excellence
- Establish and maintain exceptionally high standards for code quality, system architecture and ML research and engineering practices through hands-on coding and technical review
- Design robust, well-engineered systems that others can build upon, balancing research velocity with production requirements
- Drive technical decisions on model selection, training approaches and deployment strategies
Deliver high-impact AI projects across diverse domains
- Develop and deploy AI solutions across the entire technology development pipeline- computational chemistry simulations, agentic workflows and beyond
- Rapidly upskill in new technical areas through close collaboration with domain experts (no prior chemistry or materials experience required)
- Demonstrate strong implementation skills through hands-on development, contributing significantly to the codebase
- Balance research rigour with pragmatic engineering to deliver production-ready systems at scale
Push the frontier of ML research
- Design and implement novel ML architectures for complex scientific domains, with work that meets publication standards at top-tier conferences
- Drive research projects from conception through to deployment, showing initiative and technical depth
- Engage continuously with the latest ML literature, staying current with developments in foundation models, generative AI and scientific machine learning
What We're Looking For
- Significant software engineering and ML experience, with depth in training, evaluating and deploying AI models - demonstrated through industry work
- Proven experience training, evaluating and productionising AI models at scale, with deep understanding of the full ML lifecycle from research to deployment
- Strong engineering fundamentals with the ability to write high-quality, maintainable code and architect robust systems
- A strong ability to reason about algorithms, system design, linear algebra, probabilistic concepts and ML engineering trade-offs
- An ability to debug complex machine learning systems through meticulous attention to detail, testing of edge cases and carefully selected ablations
- A genuine interest in building AI systems that enable breakthrough scientific and industrial applications
- Upon reading Hamming's You and Your Research, you resonate with quotes such as:
- "Yes, I would like to do first-class work"
- "You should do your job in such a fashion that others can build on top of it, so they will indeed say, 'Yes, I've stood on so and so's shoulders and I saw further.'"
- "Instead of attacking isolated problems, I made the resolution that I would never again solve an isolated problem except as characteristic of a class"
Bonus: Experience with physics-informed or chemistry-focused AI applications. Experience building or fine-tuning large language models. Experience with agent-based systems, tool use or agentic workflows. Contributions to open-source ML projects or published research.
Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Platform
text:
Orbital Industries is building the AI Industrial: a new category of company that solves the physical world's hardest problems with frontier AI.
Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system for science and engineering. CurieOS connects three disciplines that have historically worked in silos — materials discovery, hardware product development and deployment engineering — into a single AI orchestration platform. No other company operates across this full lifecycle.
We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.
Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.
The role
Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced.
The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do.
This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is.
How we work
We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out.
You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production.
What you'll work on first
In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you:
- Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews.
- Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on.
- Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. A model or prompt change should have to pass the same gate as a code change.
- Observability and cost. Knowing the platform is healthy and what it costs. That means SLOs, tracing and alerting, plus cost telemetry and usage metering for every workflow and every customer, so we can see where model and compute spend goes and make deliberate choices about it.
- Infrastructure and deployment. One standard for how CurieOS is deployed, configured and upgraded in each environment, across our own cloud accounts, GPU capacity and customer-dedicated deployments.
Where the platform is going
Once those foundations are solid, there's a lot to shape next:
- Traceable results. Provenance for every number an agent produces: which inputs, tools, models and versions went into it, so our users can check it and sign it off.
- Agent runtime and context. How agents plan, call tools, manage context across long-running work and hand off to people at the right moment.
- Durable workflows. Orchestration that survives failures, retries and runs lasting hours, mixing agent steps with deterministic calculations.
At Staff level, you'd set technical direction across these areas, not just within one. You'd own one of them end to end, run the design reviews that our research and forward deployed teams build on, make the architecture calls that are hard to reverse, and help shape how we hire and grow engineers.
Our stack
Python services on Kubernetes, running on AWS plus specialist GPU clouds for heavy compute. Strong engineers from Go, Kotlin, Java or a comparable stack will pick up the language quickly. What matters more is that you've run real systems in the cloud.
You'll have most of these
- Designed and built backend services that other teams or customers relied on, and made the key decisions yourself.
- Owned a system in production after it shipped: the cloud infrastructure it ran on, on-call, incidents, how changes went out, and the monitoring that told you it was healthy.
- Built and run something where LLMs do real work for real users, and dealt with the cost, latency and quality trade-offs that come with it.
- Used coding agents heavily in your own work, with opinions on where they help and where they break.
- Led a project end to end, made trade-offs you can explain, and raised the bar for the engineers around you.
Bonus points
- Shipped software to external enterprise customers: SSO, tenant isolation, per-customer deployments, security reviews.
- Run infrastructure as code at scale, or GPU workloads across more than one cloud provider.
- Helped a system or a company through a scaling phase, such as a platform going from internal use to many external customers.
- Worked closely with researchers, scientists, engineers or other domain experts and built what they actually needed.
- For Staff: a track record of setting technical direction beyond your own team, such as architecture other teams adopted, a migration you led across several teams, or engineers you've grown into senior roles.
You don't need a background in materials, chemistry or engineering. You'll pick up the domain from the people who have it.
Why Orbital
Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company. We put frontier AI into the making of critical physical products, from advanced materials to data-centre engineering. Our research team works at the cutting edge, from universal interatomic potentials to GPU-native simulation, and we turn that research into tools engineers use every day. CurieOS is the platform that brings it together: the AI operating system the whole company runs on, which customers are starting to depend on for their own engineering work too.
Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

text:

Role Overview
You'll own the day-to-day operation of Orbital's next-generation Direct-to-Chip test rigs — running the tests, troubleshooting the hardware, and turning raw rig output into data the engineering team can act on. Starting with the final design of our tray-level test rig, you'll take it through component selection, build and commissioning, then do it again with a full rack-scale validation unit..
Key Responsibilities
Test Rig Operation
- Lead day-to-day operation of our tray and rack level engineering test and validation rigs
- Plan, set up and execute test campaigns against engineering requirements
- Troubleshoot rig faults and drive them to resolution
Data Review and Analysis
- Carry out preliminary review of test data for quality and validity
- Feed clean, well-structured data into our analysis pipelines
- Report findings back to the engineering team and flag anomalies early
- Propose next steps to drive system efficiency
Rig design, Build and Commissioning
- Contribute to the final design of tray and rack level test rigs
- Size, identify and procure key rig components, managing suppliers and lead times
- Build and commission rigs, including leak checks and function testing
Instrumentation and Electrical
- Install and wire thermocouples, sensors and signal instrumentation
- Support mechanical and electrical builds, including control panels, under the guidance of our mechanical and electrical leads
- Verify sensor calibration and signal integrity before test
What We’re Looking For
- Experience operating test rigs or lab hardware, ideally in a thermal, fluids or electronics cooling context
- Confident with data — able to spot bad readings, sanity-check results and structure output for downstream analysis
- Comfortable with low-voltage wiring, thermocouples and sensor signals
- Practical troubleshooter who works the problem on the rig rather than from a desk
- Able to size and specify components and see procurement through to delivery
- Hands-on capability with 3D printers, CNC or workshop tooling is a genuine bonus
Why Join Orbital?
- Competitive salary and equity package - the ability to own part of Orbital as we grow
- Flexible and generous paid time off
- Excellent health, dental and vision insurance plan
- Regular company offsites
- The experience of working in a cutting-edge organisation dedicated to a better future

Role Overview
We're hiring Founding Sales (Science) to win and grow enterprise customers for CurieOS across the scientific sector.
This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own the full sales cycle, from first conversation to signed enterprise license. You'll sell to a specific group of buyers: scientific R&D organisations (chemicals, advanced materials, life sciences and energy). Most employ thousands of people.
CurieOS is an operating system for science and engineering. Scientists and engineers give it multi-step, goal-driven instructions. CurieOS then runs literature review, atomistic simulation with Orb, data analysis, engineering design and hardware specification. BASF already licenses CurieOS for catalyst R&D in automotive emissions.
Timing matters. Large R&D and engineering organisations are deciding now how agentic AI fits into their work, and interest in CurieOS from leading companies is strong. You'll convert this opportunity into enterprise contracts by building pipeline, developing strategic relationships and closing complex deals. You'll bring the experience to qualify, price, negotiate and grow enterprise platform partnerships.
You'll be one of the first dedicated commercial hires for CurieOS. You'll work directly with the founders, GTM and Product teams, and our own scientists and engineers who use and build CurieOS every day.
Key Responsibilities
Win New Enterprise Customers
- Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through technical evaluation, pilot and close
- Convert inbound interest from the largest enterprises in our sectors, and build outbound pipeline into the next tier of target accounts
- Close six- and seven-figure platform agreements, managing buying committees across R&D, engineering, IT security, procurement and legal
Sell Across Key Customers
- Sell to scientific R&D buyers: computational chemists, materials scientists and R&D directors at chemicals, materials, life sciences and energy companies.
- Open new customers with a focused first deployment in R&D, then expand across the business to the engineering teams that turn those materials into products.
- Show buyers clearly why an agentic operating system built for science and engineering does what general-purpose AI assistants cannot
Run Technical Evaluations That Convert
- Agree pilot success criteria, owners and timelines with the customer before work begins
- Lead technical discovery and demos yourself, and work with our forward-deployed engineers and scientists on drive adoption
- Clear security and data-governance reviews, covering IP protection, data residency and model governance
Set the Standard for Enterprise Sales
- Bring the enterprise sales discipline a fast-moving team needs: qualification, forecasting, pricing, contracting and pilot structure. Build the CurieOS sales playbook as you go
- Expand first deployments into multi-team and multi-site enterprise licenses
- Turn customer outcomes into references and case studies that shorten the next sales cycle
What We’re Looking For
- You know the market for science technologies. You've sold directly into scientific R&D in chemicals, materials or life sciences. You know how each sector buys. You also know how large enterprises work: security review, procurement, legal, and the IP and data-security demands that come with them. You already have a network among R&D and engineering leaders at large enterprises.
- You've closed large, complex technical deals. You've sold technical platforms to technical buyers. That could be scientific software, simulation and CAE, R&D informatics, HPC or AI/ML. You've closed six- and seven-figure deals at revenue-stage companies and hit quota consistently. We're hiring for proven experience, not potential. Experience selling AI or agentic products, or building a sales motion at an early-stage company, is a plus. Nobody has sold CurieOS before, so you'll be winning new logos without a playbook.
- You build credibility with scientific audiences. Senior scientists and engineering leaders take you seriously from the first meeting. You can run discovery with a computational chemist and an engineering lead in the same week. You use AI every day in your own work. A STEM degree or scientific background is strongly preferred.
Why Join Orbital Industries?
- Competitive salary and equity package - the ability to own part of Orbital Industries as we grow
- Flexible and generous paid time off
- Excellent health, dental and vision insurance plan
- Regular company offsites to the USA and beyond
- The chance to define the narrative for a new category — the AI Industrial — at a company where communications is a strategic function, not a support one
Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Role Overview
Orbital Industries' AI software platform, CurieOS, is used by scientists and engineers to design and build products serving critical industries. Powering this software are our own frontier AI models in advanced materials, hardware engineering and simulation.
As a Deployment Strategist at Orbital Industries, you will work with chemistry, materials and pharma customers to find out where CurieOS can create real value, then build the solutions that deliver it. You will dig into each customer's problems, understand their science and their business, and turn what you learn into applications on CurieOS that their scientists and engineers use every day.
The role combines consultancy and product building. You will spend your time with customer R&D teams and decision-makers, framing problems, shaping solutions and measuring the business impact they deliver. We want someone who is commercially sharp, scientifically grounded and motivated by results customers can see.
Key Responsibilities
Understand the customer and their problem space
- Embed with customer R&D teams in chemistry, materials and pharma to understand their workflows, constraints and commercial priorities
- Question customers rigorously: challenge assumptions, get to the root of the problem and identify where CurieOS can have the most impact
- Build trusted relationships with scientists, R&D leaders and business stakeholders, acting as their strategic partner throughout the engagement
Design and build solutions customers believe in
- Translate customer needs into clear solution designs, then build applications and workflows on CurieOS that solve them
- Bring strong UX sensibility to everything you build, so solutions are intuitive and fit naturally into how scientists and engineers work
- Iterate closely with customers until they agree the solution is right, working with Orbital Industries' engineering and research teams where deeper technical work is needed
Drive and measure business impact
- Own each engagement end-to-end, from scoping and success criteria through delivery and adoption
- Define and track the business outcomes that matter to the customer, such as time-to-discovery, experiments avoided, design-cycle reduction and cost savings, and communicate results to senior stakeholders
- Find opportunities to expand engagements, partnering with the commercial team to grow accounts
- Turn what works into repeatable playbooks and solution templates, and feed customer insight back into the CurieOS roadmap
What We’re Looking For
- A grounding in chemistry, materials science or pharma, whether through study, research or industry work, with enough depth to engage credibly with customers
- A track record of building solutions for industry and measuring their business impact
- Strong consultative skills: you can question customers, frame ambiguous problems and guide stakeholders to a solution they agree on
- Commercial acumen, with an understanding of how R&D decisions connect to business value
- The ability to turn customer needs into working solutions, with a strong sense for user experience and good design
- Comfort with technical tools and enough technical fluency to build applications on a software platform and work closely with engineers
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage everyone from scientists to executives
- The ability to succeed in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where requirements change as you work directly with customers
Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

This is a category-creation brief. You'll articulate what the AI Industrial is, why CurieOS matters, and how Orbital Industries' full-lifecycle approach (materials, engineering, hardware) represents something genuinely new. You'll translate deep technical work - across AI, materials science, and hardware engineering - into clear, distinctive, high-quality communication that builds authority with investors, technical buyers, talent, and the broader market.
Your job is to set the strategic direction: brand voice, messaging frameworks, content strategy, and open doors for media.
Key Responsibilities
Communications Strategy and Brand Voice
- Define and own Orbital Industries' external communications strategy — how we are positioned, perceived, and understood in the market
- Build and enforce consistency in brand voice across all external channels: website, social, events, collateral, press
- Set the messaging framework for CurieOS and its three pillars (Materials, Deployment, Hardware), ensuring our full-lifecycle positioning is sharp and differentiated
- Write strong creative and messaging briefs for design, video, and campaign work — giving the GTM team clear strategic direction to execute against
- Ensure a clean separation between Orbital Industries (brand authority, category definition) and Orbital IT (commercial, customer-facing) in how we communicate externally
Stakeholder messaging
- Work closely with the CFO and founders to ensure investor messaging reflects Orbital Industries' positioning as the AI Industrial category leader, not just a product company
- Translate technical milestones (CurieOS releases, customer deployments, materials breakthroughs) into compelling narratives
Content and copy
- Own long-form writing, thought leadership, website messaging, investor content, and campaign assets - from strategy through to production
- Produce content that makes Orbital Industries' work in AI, materials science and hardware engineering accessible without losing credibility or nuance — you know the difference between simplifying and dumbing down
- Develop and maintain CurieOS content across its three pillars: materials discovery, deployment engineering, and hardware product development
- Use LLMs and modern tools to work efficiently while maintaining high editorial standards
Social Media Strategy
- Own organic social strategy: voice, editorial calendar, content direction and output quality
- Build Orbital Industries' social presence into a distinctive point of view, not just a broadcast channel — the GTM team handles day-to-day posting and scheduling
- Track developments across AI infrastructure and adjacent industries to keep content timely and credible
- Partner with the GTM Lead to align organic and paid social messaging
Website messaging
- Own website copy and landing-page messaging, ensuring it is sharp, current and aligned to business priorities
- Work closely with the GTM team on copy for campaign landing pages — you own the message, they own the conversion optimisation and testing cycle
Press and Media
- Develop Orbital Industries' press function - strengthening media relationships, identifying opportunities, and positioning the company for coverage that reinforces our authority in the AI Industrial category
- Amplify founder positioning for external audiences, interviews, speaking engagements and media appearances
- Manage freelance press support and scale the function as the company grows

- Significant leadership experience in communications, content, editorial or brand storytelling — ideally in a technical, deep-tech or science-adjacent environment. Experience with investor communications or fundraising narratives is a strong plus
- An excellent writer with strong editorial taste and clear judgement; your portfolio should demonstrate range across long-form, short-form and messaging work
- Deep curiosity about AI, science, engineering or technical products — you follow these spaces because you're genuinely interested, not because it's your job
- The ability to make technical ideas accessible without losing credibility or nuance
- Comfortable owning both strategy and execution — you can set the direction, produce the work, and build the systems that maintain quality without you touching every piece
- Experience building or significantly expanding a communications function — you should find creating something from scratch exciting, not uncomfortable
- High standards for writing, messaging, and brand consistency — you notice when things drift and you fix them before they compound
- Strong collaborative instincts — you'll work closely with technical founders, engineers, a GTM Lead, a design function. You need to influence without owning every channel
- Experience briefing and managing creative work: design, video, freelance writers, press agencies
- Science degree or background is preferred
Why Join Orbital Industries?
- Competitive salary and equity package - the ability to own part of Orbital Industries as we grow
- Flexible and generous paid time off
- Excellent health, dental and vision insurance plan
- Regular company offsites to the USA and beyond
- The chance to define the narrative for a new category — the AI Industrial — at a company where communications is a strategic function, not a support one

- Close six- and seven-figure platform agreements, managing buying committees across R&D, engineering, IT security, procurement and legal
Sell Across Key Customers
- Sell to scientific R&D buyers: computational chemists, materials scientists and R&D directors at chemicals, materials, life sciences and energy companies.
- Open new customers with a focused first deployment in R&D, then expand across the business to the engineering teams that turn those materials into products.
- Show buyers clearly why an agentic operating system built for science and engineering does what general-purpose AI assistants cannot
Run Technical Evaluations That Convert
- Agree pilot success criteria, owners and timelines with the customer before work begins
- Lead technical discovery and demos yourself, and work with our forward-deployed engineers and scientists on drive adoption
- Clear security and data-governance reviews, covering IP protection, data residency and model governance
Set the Standard for Enterprise Sales
- Bring the enterprise sales discipline a fast-moving team needs: qualification, forecasting, pricing, contracting and pilot structure. Build the CurieOS sales playbook as you go
- Expand first deployments into multi-team and multi-site enterprise licenses
- Turn customer outcomes into references and case studies that shorten the next sales cycle
What We’re Looking For
- You know the market for science technologies. You've sold directly into scientific R&D in chemicals, materials or life sciences. You know how each sector buys. You also know how large enterprises work: security review, procurement, legal, and the IP and data-security demands that come with them. You already have a network among R&D and engineering leaders at large enterprises.

You've closed six- and seven-figure deals at revenue-stage companies and hit quota consistently. We're hiring for proven experience, not potential. Experience selling AI or agentic products, or building a sales motion at an early-stage company, is a plus. Nobody has sold CurieOS before, so you'll be winning new logos without a playbook.
- You build credibility with scientific audiences. Senior scientists and engineering leaders take you seriously from the first meeting. You can run discovery with a computational chemist and an engineering lead in the same week. You use AI every day in your own work. A STEM degree or scientific background is strongly preferred.

title: Supply Chain Manager
text:
Orbital Industries is building the AI Industrial: a new category of company that solves the physical world's hardest problems with frontier AI.
Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system for science and engineering. CurieOS connects three disciplines that have historically worked in silos — materials discovery, hardware product development and deployment engineering — into a single AI orchestration platform. No other company operates across this full lifecycle.
We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.
Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.
Role Overview
We are hiring a Supply Chain Manager to manage the end-to-end sourcing and delivery operations. You will coordinate our global network of OEMs, fabricators, and critical equipment suppliers to move designs from engineering into production scale.
This role spans specialty cooling fluids and cold plates,through to critical power, cooling equipment . You will actively use and help build AI-enabled supply chain tools in CurieOS, feeding real-world supplier constraints, lead times, and manufacturing data back into our team to accelerate every build cycle.
Key Responsibilities
- Unified Sourcing & Vendor Orchestration: Build and manage a resilient global supplier ecosystem spanning our full technology stack from DTC liquid cooling hardware (cold plates, CDUs, manifolds and proprietary coolants) to long-lead data center power, cooling, and modular equipment (CRAHs, switchgear, UPS, PDUs, and prefabricated modules).
- Engineering-to-Scale Execution : Partner directly with thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to bridge early prototypes, test rigs, and machine shops into volume OEM production.
- Delivery & Production Scheduling: Own vendor capacity planning and global logistics to hit PO-to-deployment timelines.
- Procurement Operations & Compliance: Own day-to-day purchasing execution, including RFQs, Purchase Orders, NDAs, and vendor onboarding, while driving competitive quoting, cost tracking, dual-sourcing options, and technical compliance (such as UL/ETL certifications) alongside legal and leadership.
What We’re Looking For
- You have helped get physical products made, whether in supply chain, operations, manufacturing or product development.
- You are comfortable managing product BOMs and contract manufacturers
- You are experienced in procuring long-lead equipment, reviewing vendor submittals, and coordinating site deliveries.
- You are able to read engineering drawings and BOMs, track UL/ETL and quality milestones, and run tight RFQ-to-PO workflows with OEMs and specialty fabricators
- You thrive in a startup and already use AI in your daily work.
Why Join Orbital Industries?
- Competitive salary and equity package - the ability to own part of Orbital as we grow
- Flexible and generous paid time off
- Excellent health, dental and vision insurance plan
- Regular company offsites
- The experience of working in a cutting-edge organisation dedicated to a better future
